metadados.title: PRISM Scale - Pediatric Risk of Mortality
metadados.description: The PRISM (Pediatric Risk of Mortality) is a severity assessment scale used in pediatric intensive care units (PICU) to estimate the risk of mortality in hospitalized children.

secoes.corpo:
Based on detected pediatric physiological changes.

Processing clinical reasoning...

A NANDA diagnosis requires a careful evaluation of its taxonomies and the search for defining characteristics and related factors. The disclosure of diagnoses on this scale serves only an educational purpose, to promote its use and help users become familiar with the various diagnoses. Under no circumstances should it induce the user to indiscriminately apply any nursing diagnosis without the support of clinical findings obtained through history taking, physical examination, and other systematic tools that will guide the nurse in prescribing care.

Score Interpretation

Low Risk (0-5 points)
Reduced risk of mortality, organ failure absent or mild.

Moderate Risk (6-15 points)
Intermediate risk. Presence of dysfunctions requiring monitoring.

High Risk (16-20 points)
Multiple organ failure. Intensive intervention needed.

Very High Risk (> 20 points)
Extremely high risk of mortality. Severe and irreversible dysfunction.
